Answer: C
Reason: The axial CT image shows an ill-defined soft tissue mass/infiltrate located centrally in the mediastinum adjacent to the trachea, which correlates with the clinical symptoms of dysphonia and is consistent with a primary tracheal or central airway malignancy like squamous cell carcinoma. Peripheral nodules (A, B) or cardiac findings (F) do not explain the central airway involvement suggested by the hoarseness.
